fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain clear vehicle-width clearance for emergency apparatus.
• Clear a direct walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move quickly between both buildings.
• Post the address number visibly at the detached structure so responders can identify it as a separate building.
• Keep all gates and access points unlocked or fitted with a key lockbox accessible to emergency responders.
• Trim dense vegetation away from walkways connecting the front entry to parking and side areas so responders can move on foot without obstruction.
• Mark or identify all access points to the property so arriving responders can quickly determine available entry routes.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear enough to allow emergency apparatus to turn around or stage without being blocked.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to give responders clear visibility of all sides of the building.
• Identify and mark any ground-level hazards such as low posts, drainage edges, or landscape borders in areas where responders may move in low visibility conditions.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to increase open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees near the structure to reduce the ability of fire to climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Clear shrubs and other plants growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Keep the area beneath tree clusters free of dead leaves, fallen branches, and other dry plant material.
• Maintain separation between the edges of tree clusters and any outbuildings or storage areas on the property.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
